public_chronology:
PUBLIC CHRONOLOGY — VERDANT HARBOR

The civilian departure restriction, Order V-17, followed the first attack.

This is the account displayed here today. A summary is not an independent second source.

registers.1:
CLINIC REGISTER — STORM EVENING

The clinic courtyard was opened as temporary shelter. The working entry refers to the civilian departure restriction already in force under Order V-17. Its storm-evening entry precedes the first attack in the public chronology.

This surviving register records a restriction in use. It does not identify who issued the original order or why.
registers.2:
HARBOR DEPARTURE RECORD — STORM EVENING

The waiting shelter remained usable. The departure clerk recorded civilian passage being restricted under Order V-17. Its storm-evening entry precedes the first attack in the public chronology.

This surviving departure record records a restriction in use. It does not identify who issued the original order or why.

comparison:
COMPARISON

The displayed chronology places V-17 after the first attack. This newly preserved record applies V-17 on an earlier storm evening. Was a storm precaution extended, the public chronology mistaken, or an earlier decision later relabeled?

NEXT LEAD: Find the original Order V-17: issuer, time, and stated purpose. The discrepancy is a question, not proof of a conspiracy.

return_common: I kept waiting for everything to look different.

OPEN QUESTION
Find the original Order V-17, its issuer, time and purpose. An inconsistent chronology does not establish a motive or identify a culprit.
